To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized luminescent polymer ligands and divalent europium complexes with polymer ligand.

the luminescence efficiency of the polymer ligands containing cryptands as the chelating units is high, and that the luminescent properties of the polymer ligand are affected by the size and the structure of cryptand units.
the luminescent properties of divalent europium complexes of polymer ligands containing (2.2.2) and ( 2.2. 1) cryptand units were investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of polymer ligands containing cryptand units and the preparation of luminescent Eu2+-complexes.
the synthesis and characterization of a novel class of luminescent polymers, which are based on a europium complex with a polymer containing (2.2,2) and (21.2.1)cryptand units.
luminescent materials for use as optical devices such as optical fibers, optical amplifiers and optical switches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymer ligands are effective in forming luminescent Eu2+ complexes and the complexes are useful in luminescence applications
Eu2+ cryptates have high emission efficiencies, and that the luminescence efficiency of Eu2+ cryptate-attacking polymers is high.

Eu2+ complexes of polymer ligands containing (2.2,2) and (22.1) cryptand units are promising luminescent materials for applications such as luminescent labels, sensors and luminescent solar concentrators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Eu2+ complexes with polymer ligand containing [2.2. 2] cryptand unit have high luminescence quantum yields and the Eu2+ complex of polymer ligand containing a [2.2.1] cryptand unit had the highest luminescence intensity.

the Eu2+-cryptate complexation in the polymers has a great effect on the luminescence intensity, and the luminescence efficiency is improved with the decrease in the number of cryptand units in the ligand.
the Eu2+ ion can be used to emit luminescence in a wide range of polymers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the luminescence efficiency of Eu2+-cryptate-attaching polymers is higher than that of the corresponding Eu3+-cryptate-attached polymers.
Eu2+ complexes of cryptand-containing polymer ligands can be used as luminescence labels.
the polymer complexes of Eu2+ are luminescent.
